newsitem.title: INDIA: India contracts 350,000T soymeal sales for Nov-Jan.
newsitem.headline: India contracts 350,000T soymeal sales for Nov-Jan.

text.p: India has signed contracts for 350,000 tonnes of soymeal exports for November-January shipments, traders said on Friday.
They said demand for Indian soymeal from China and some other countries had increased due to its high 48 percent protein content compared to 44 percent in soymeal from other origins.
Traders last week said contracts for nearly 300,000 tonnes of soymeal exports had been signed.
"International demand for Indian soymeal is very strong for its high protein content," said Prakash Mutha, a leading oilmeal trader.
Traders said Singapore-based Peter Cremer had bought 110,000 tonnes, Germany's Toepfer International 70,000 tonnes while the Hong Kong-based Concordia bought 50,000 tonnes.
Cargill Hong Kong Ltd had contracted for 30,000 tonnes while Singapore's G. Premjee had bought 25,000 tonnes, they said.
Details of the remaining deals were not available.
The main Indian sellers were OILFED, Gujrat Ambuja Protein Ltd, Ruchi Soya Industries, Prestige Foods and the State Trading Corporation, they said.
Indian yellow soymeal is quoted at $300-301 per tonne FAS for September-October shipments compared with $185-188 per tonne at the start of the season last November.
Soymeal contracts for November, December and January shipments were quoted at $280-281 per tonne.
